review_scope: Read every byte of all five submitted Python sources, common TASK.md, README.md, manifest.json, evaluator runner and probe; verified reviewed copies byte-identical. No candidate code imported or executed. No candidate-owned dependencies beyond the reviewed module; imports use existing Python standard library. Standard library/runtime is trusted, not a line-by-line re-audit.
top_level_effects: Only a module docstring, standard-library imports, three integer constants, and function/class definitions. No candidate I/O or computations with external effects at import.
filesystem_review: All candidate persistence functions construct paths from the explicit root supplied by frozen probe; fixture paths remain under work_root/tmp. Temporary files use dir=self.root. Candidate file effects are mkdir/stat/lstat/open/read/write/close/replace/unlink within those roots. Snapshot/root final symlink checks use no-follow behavior. No network, credential, subprocess, environment lookup or dynamic code execution in candidate sources.
harness_review: Frozen probe imports only the reviewed source, runs the same ordered 13 checks for every trial, creates owned temporary fixtures including symlinks and a FIFO solely under work_root/tmp, removes fixtures, and writes its JSON result under work_root. Its monkeypatches affect only local os replacement functions/direct module aliases. Runner creates exactly one child process per plan with -I/-B and a reduced environment. No reference/control execution paths used.
concerns: This is source-reviewed bounded local execution, not OS/process/network isolation. Limits are backstops, not containment.

Static protected-input lookup is unreadable for flattened frozen artifact paths because TASK.md and inputs are not included at the inferred parent. Do not convert this packaging issue into a rubric failure. Existing collection receipts report protected files unchanged; common authored TASK.md independently matches its manifest.
Candidate self-reported local test counts in collection receipts are not independently verified and do not contribute to primary scores.
Frozen probe catches general exceptions as fail. Any observed denial, infrastructure error, interrupted run or timeout must remain not assessed rather than be promoted to a rubric failure.
Candidate merge complexity can be quadratic, but frozen probes are small and bounded; no post-hoc stress probes are proposed.
